Enantioselective Synthesis
Diastereoselective and Enantioselective Hydrophosphinylations of
Conjugated Enynes, Allenes and Dienes via Synergistic Pd/Co
Catalysis
Ming-Qiao Tang, Zi-Jiang Yang, Ai-Jun Han, and Zhi-Tao He*
Abstract: Different from the reported work focusing on
the construction of single P- or C-stereocenter via
hydrophosphinylation of unsaturated carbon bonds, the
highly diastereo- and enantioselective hydrophosphiny-
lation reaction of allenes, conjugated enynes and 1,3-
dienes is achieved via a designed Pd/Co dual catalysis
and newly modified masked phosphinylating reagent. A
series of allyl motifs bearing both a tertiary C- and
P-stereocenter are prepared in generally good yields,
> 20 : 1 dr, > 20 : 1 rr and 99 % ee. The unprecedented
diastereo- and enantioselective hydrophosphinylation of
1,3-enynes is established to generate skeletons contain-
ing both a P-stereocenter and a nonadjacent chiral axis.
The first stereodivergent hydrophosphinylation reaction
is also developed to achieve all four P-containing stereo-
isomers. The present protocol features the use of only
3-minutes reaction time and 0.1 % catalyst, and with the
observation of up to 730 TON. A set of mechanistic
studies reveal the necessity and roles of two metal
catalysts and corroborate the designed synergistic proc-
ess.
Introduction
Enantioenriched organophosphorus motifs have been widely
used in chiral ligand and catalyst design, medicinal and
material chemistry.
[1]
In addition to various catalytic path-
ways such as 1,4-conjugate addition, allylic substitution,
cross coupling, nucleophilic substitution and others,
[2]
the
asymmetric hydrophosphinylation and hydrophosphination
of unsaturated carbon-carbon bonds have emerged as a
valuable and convenient route to construct these
skeletons.
[3–9]
For example, in 2018, Dong reported the first
Pd-catalyzed asymmetric hydrophosphinylation of unacti-
vated 1,3-dienes.
[4b]
Wang and Li extended hydrophosphina-
tion and hydrophosphinylation to the use of allenes with
high enantiocontrol.
[4h,i]
However, these works focus exclu-
sively on the construction of P- or C-stereocenter and fail to
provide high stereocontrol on both of them simultaneously
(Scheme 1a). A few prior works tried to establish the related
diastereoselective processes but generally furnished 1 : 1
diastereoselectivity for the transformations.
[4h,l,5b,f,8]
Only an
elegant work by Li and co-workers describes diastereoselec-
tive access to phosphine-functionalized olefins via Pd-
catalyzed hydrophosphination of alkynes.
[4i]
Thus, the route
to achieve diastereo- and enantioselective hydrophosphiny-
lation and hydrophosphination reactions is still rare. Mean-
while, the asymmetric hydrofunctionalization of 1,3-enynes
is a facile route to prepare enantioenriched allenes,
[10,11]
but
related hydrophosphinylation and hydrophosphination proc-
esses remain undeveloped, neither enantioselectively nor
diastereoselectively.
Stereodivergent synthesis has received much attention
due to the potential to achieve all the stereoisomers of a
constructed skeleton.
[12]
However, all the reported studies
focus on the construction of C-based stereocenters, and
seldomly explore the involvement of heteroatom-based
stereocenter (Scheme 1b). Obviously, heteroatom-based
stereodivergent synthesis represents a new direction in this
area and would greatly extend the concept of stereo-
divergent synthesis. Therefore, stereodivergent hydrophos-
phinylation and hydrophosphination reaction to prepare P-
involved chiral motifs are unknown.
Synergistic catalysis has shown great potential in control-
ling multiple stereocenters in the stereoselective synthesis.
[13]
Recently, Duan et al. reported an interesting study toward
the preparation of P-stereocenter via Co-catalyzed 1,4-
addition and nucleophilic substitution with racemic
phosphine oxides.
[14]
Inspired by this work and considering
the high efficiency of Pd-catalyzed asymmetric
hydrofunctionalizations,
[15–18]
we envisioned that a synergistic
Pd/Co catalytic system might provide a novel solution to this
long-standing unsolved diastereoselective hydrophosphiny-
lation to construct motifs bearing both a P- and C-stereo-
center. Meanwhile, with the precise dictation of Pd and Co
catalysts on related coupling partners, the stereodivergent

ing stereoisomers might also be realized for the first time.
Herein, we describe our endeavors to establish three
types of diastereo- and enantioselective hydrophosphinyla-
tion transformations via a synergistic Pd/Co catalysis
(Scheme 1c). With allene and newly modified masked P(V)
reagent as the substrates, the hydrophosphinylation can be
realized to generate skeletons bearing both a P- and
C-stereocenter. The hydrophosphinylation of 1,3-enynes is
also developed to furnish motifs containing a P-stereocenter
and a chiral axis. This protocol is further applied to the
unprecedented diastereoselective hydrophosphinylation of
conjugated diene. In addition, a stereodivergent protocol is
described to access all of the stereoisomers of the con-
structed P-containing units.
Results and Discussion
With this design in mind, aryloxyallene 1 a and pyridyl
phosphine oxide 2 a-1 were selected as the electrophile and
nucleophile, respectively (Table 1). When BINAP L5 was
selected as the chiral ligand for Pd catalyst, a set of chiral
ligands for Co metal was evaluated first. With Boxmi ligand
L1 used,
[19]
the synergistic catalysis occurred and provided
3 a in 36 % yield and 60 % ee but with 1.4 : 1 dr (entry 1).
When a similar ligand L2 was used instead, both the
reactivity and stereocontrol were increased obviously. In
this case, 77 % yield, 4.5 : 1 dr and 79 % ee for product 3 a
were observed (entry 2). Other chiral ligands did not show
better stereocontrol for the hydrofunctionalization process
(see Supporting Information for details). Next, a group of
chiral ligands instead of L5 for Pd metal was checked
(entries 3–9). Among them, L10 exhibited the optimal
results, furnishing 3 a in 75 % yield, 11 : 1 dr and 96 % ee. A
series of other condition evaluations including different
bases and solvents were conducted. The corresponding
results were summarized in the Supporting Information but
all failed to provide superior effects.
Murakami et al. demonstrated that an α-hydroxyalkyl-
phosphonate as the masked phosphonating reagent could
prevent catalyst deactivation and presumably have a positive
influence on reactivity and selectivity.
[20]
Several modified
P(V) reagents 2 a, 2 a-2 and 2 a-3 were thus synthesized from
the reaction of 2 a-1 and ketones. We found that these new
phosphonating reagents are actually much easier to be
prepared and purified than that for 2 a-1. With 2 a used
instead of 2 a-1 (entry 10), indeed both the diastereoselectiv-
ity and enantioselectivity of 3 a were elevated (from 11 : 1 to
> 20 : 1 dr and 96 % to 97 % ee). Similarly, 2 a-2 and 2 a-3 as
masked 2 a-1 showed excellent stereocontrol effects and
with slightly decreased yields for 3 a (entries 11–12). When
the reaction temperature was lowered to room temperature,
3 a was achieved in the highest 71 % yield, > 20 : 1 dr and
> 99 % ee (entry 13), and the conditions used in this reaction
were thus determined to be the optimal conditions for the
diastereoselective hydrophosphinylation process. It should
be noted that, in this context, if ent-L2 was adopted instead
of L2, both the diastereoselectivity and enantioselectivity of
3 a decreased heavily (entry 14). This fact suggested the
importance of selecting matched chiral ligands for corre-
sponding two metal catalysts.
The scope of allene substrates was first evaluated, and
the results are summarized in Scheme 2. The aryloxyallene 1
bearing substituents with diverse electronic and steric
characters showed good tolerance with the hydrophosphiny-
lation reaction. In general, around 70 % yield, > 20 : 1 dr,
> 20 : 1 rr and 99 % ee were provided for the allyl phosphine

Estradiol valerate-derived allene substrate was compatible
with the reaction (3 n), indicating the potential power of the
present method for late-stage modification of complex
molecules. In addition, the arene containing two allene units
underwent double diastereoselective hydrophosphinylation
processes and was transformed into a single stereoisomer
3 o. The absolute configuration of 3 e was elucidated to be
(R,R)-3 e via the X-ray crystallography analyses.
The scope of unsymmetric phosphine oxide nucleophiles
was next checked by preparing a series of stable P(V)
precursors 2. The corresponding results are summarized in
Scheme 3. The substituents at different positions of pyridyl
unit in the phosphine oxide 2 did not exhibit discernible
influence on the reaction, generating 3 p–3 s in 64–86 % yield
and with generally > 20 : 1 dr, > 20 : 1 rr and > 94 % ee. When
the phenyl unit in the P(V) reagent was replaced by a
heteroaryl or substituted aryl group, the hydrophosphinyla-
tion still proceeded smoothly, generating corresponding
chiral P(V) products (3 t–3 u) in 75–85 % yield and excellent
stereocontrol.
Considering the high reactivity and stereocontrol in
hydrophosphinylation of monosubstituted allenes, more
challenging disubstituted symmetric allenes as the substrates
were evaluated next (Scheme 4, top). Such a deracemization
process has seldomly been reported in hydrophosphinylation
area. With the use of (S)-BINAP instead of L10 as the
ligand for Pd catalyst, substrate 1 underwent the enantio-
convergent hydrophosphinylation reaction smoothly, provid-
ing 4 a–4 c in moderate yield and with high diastereo-, regio-
and enantioselectivity. In addition, the present protocol
could be extended to the construction of chiral phosphine
sulfides through a one-pot diastereoselective hydrophosphi-
nylation and sulfuration process (Scheme 4, bottom), provid-
ing a concise route to achieve the seldomly studied motifs
bearing both a P

example, compound 5 a was prepared in 74 % yield, 17 : 1 dr
and 97 % ee by this strategy.
In fact, the 12-hour reaction time was not required. The
diastereoselective hydrophosphinylation process could be
finished in as short as 3 minutes with retained high reactivity
and stereocontrol. A set of cases were tested to demonstrate
this fact (Scheme 5, top). For example, the template product
3 a was prepared in 3 min with 71 % yield, > 20 : 1 dr,
> 20 : 1 rr and 97 % ee, comparable to that observed in
standard 12 h reaction time. Other cases (3 b, 3 f, 3 i, 3 j, 3 q)
with modifications on both nucleophiles and electrophiles
showed similar results.

Inspired by the high efficiency of the present protocol,
we guessed that a low catalyst loading might still provide
comparable reactivity. Indeed, when 0.05 % [Pd(allyl)Cl]
2
was adopted under standard conditions, the hydrofunction-
alization proceeded in good efficiency and excellent stereo-
selectivities (Scheme 5, bottom). For example, 3 a was
prepared in this context with 72 % yield, > 20 : 1 dr, > 20 : 1 rr
and 97 % ee. The corresponding catalyst turnover number
(TON) was as high as 720. To the best of our knowledge, no
previous work was reported with such a high efficiency for
asymmetric hydrofunctionalizations of unsaturated carbon-
carbon bonds. Both the short reaction time and low catalyst
loading showcase the power of this method.
Although the hydrofunctionalization of 1,3-enynes has
been widely studied,
[10]
the related hydrophosphinylation is
rare. With 1,3-enyne 6 as the substrate, L8 as the chiral
ligand for Pd catalyst and n-BuOH as the solvent, the
corresponding diastereo- and enantioselective hydrophos-
phinylation reaction occurred smoothly (Scheme 6). A

couple of enynes 6 bearing different substituents reacted
with 2 to afford chiral allenes 7 containing a nonadjacent P-
stereocenter in good yields with high diastereoselectivity,
regioselectivity and enantioselectivity (7 a–7 c). In addition,
other heterocycle substituent instead of pyridyl group in
phosphine oxide nucleophile was also compatible with the
protocol. For example, thiazole-substituted phosphine oxide
underwent the diastereoselective hydrophosphinylation
smoothly to provide 7 d in a reasonable yield and good
stereoselectivities.
To further show the synthetic power of the present
protocol, the unprecedented stereodivergent hydrophosphi-
nylation reaction was conducted (Scheme 6). All four stereo-
isomers of motifs bearing both a P-stereocenter and a
skipped chiral axis were obtained readily by dictating the
absolute configuration of the ligands ligated to correspond-
ing metals. In this case, the DTBM-Segphos (L9) showed
better stereochemical control than L8, providing (R,R)-7 a in
a reasonable yield and with good stereoselectivities.
Considering the good performance for diastereoselective
hydrophosphinylation of allenes and 1,3-enynes, we contin-
ued to check the feasibility of this process with relatively
inert 1,3-diene as the substrate (Scheme 6, bottom). Sim-
ilarly, no prior work focused on this transformation with 1,3-
dienes, and only enantioselective process was reported.
[4b]
With L12 instead of L10 as the chiral ligand for Pd catalyst
and 1.6 equiv. of 2 a were used, the hydrophosphinylation
reaction proceeded smoothly, providing product 9 in 53 %
yield, > 20 : 1 rr, 5.3 : 1 dr and 97 % ee.
[21]
In this case, when
2.0 equiv. of 2 a were used, product 9 was observed in 40 %
yield, 4.9 : 1 dr and 99 % ee (see Supporting Information for
details). The slightly decreased reactivity in this case was
presumably due to the coordination effect of excessive 2 a
with Pd metal.
To highlight the reliability and practical value of the
diastereoselective hydrophosphinylation reaction, a gram-
scale test and a series of downstream transformations were
carried out (Scheme 7a). When 4 mmol of 1 a was used, the
corresponding product 3 a was isolated in 0.92 g in 63 %
yield, > 20 : 1 dr, > 20 : 1 rr and > 99 % ee, comparable to that
on 0.1 mmol scale. The enantioenriched phosphine oxide 3 a
was smoothly transformed into phosphine sulfide 5 a with
Lawesson reagent. Chiral skeletons 10 and 11 were also
easily prepared from 3 a through hydrogenation and hydro-
boration-oxidation processes, respectively. In addition, the
ether structure in 3 a was readily released and protected by
an acetyl group to generate 12. An RCM reaction enabled
the preparation of 2H-chromene derivative 13 in 91 % yield,
> 20 : 1 dr and > 99 % ee. As two equivalents of phosphine
oxide were required to guarantee the high yield for the
hydrophosphinylation, we guessed that a kinetic resolution
might exist and the matched isomer of 2 a would be more
inclined to be consumed. Indeed, the recovered (S)-2 a from
the reaction of (�)-2 a and 1 a was obtained in 50 % yield
and with 96 % ee and the corresponding structure was
confirmed by X-ray analysis (Scheme 7b).
To probe the mechanism, we conducted control experi-
ments first to uncover the potential role of Pd and Co metal
in the reaction (Scheme 8a). Without the use of Co catalyst,
the hydrophosphinylation still occurred but with moderate
yield and decreased diastereo- and enantioselectivity. In this
case, the observed 1.2 : 1 dr indicated that both configura-
tions of racemic nucleophile 2 a could react with allyl Pd
species easily without cobalt. The observed 44 % ee instead
of 99 % ee in the template reaction showed that the C � P
formation step might involve the strong interaction of two
metal centers. On the other hand, no reaction occurred in
the absence of Pd catalyst, which was consistent with our
initial proposal that the present hydrofunctionalization
process was primarily catalyzed by Pd metal, and Co metal
mainly provide strengthened stereocontrol on the process.
The deuterium labelling experiments were next con-
ducted with MeOH-d as the solvent (Scheme 8b). The
corresponding product 3 a–d was obtained in 65 % yield and
with 94 % deuteration at the internal olefin. We also found

Next, competing experiments between three
sets of aryloxyallenes (1 a + 1 b, 1 b + 1 f and 1 a + 1 f) were
conducted (Scheme 8d). Based on the results, it seemed that
the electron-rich aryloxy units were only slightly favorable
to the reaction than electron-poor ones, especially consider-

in 1 f and 1 a but comparable yields observed for 3 f and 3 a
respectively. We thus deduced that the rate-limiting step in
the present hydrophosphinylation might not involve obvious
charge change, consistent with the neutral reductive elimi-
nation process as the rate-limiting step.
[22]
Finally, when the recovered (S)-2 a in Scheme 7b was
used as the substrate to react with 1 a under standard
conditions but with Pd/ent-L10 and Co/ent-L2 as the
catalysts, the enantiomer of 3 a was obtained in comparable
yields and stereoselectivities to that in Scheme 7b (see
Supporting Information for details). This result corrobo-
rated the fact that the matched (R)-2 a was selectively
transformed into 3 a in Scheme 7b. The same absolute
configuration of P-stereocenter in the matched nucleophile
(R)-2 a and product 3 a also suggested that the configuration
of P-stereocenter would not change during the hydrophos-
phinylation.
Based on all these facts and prior work,
[4]
a possible
catalytic cycle was postulated in Scheme 8e. Pd(0) might be
first oxidized to form PdH species, which then reacted allene
to generate allyl Pd complex int-1. Meanwhile, the Co metal
coordinated with phosphine oxide 2 a and then provided int-
3 under base, during which the matched isomer of 2 a was
preferred to be coordinated. Next, a transmetallation
process occurred between int-1 and int-3 to provide int-4.
Finally, a reductive elimination process proceeded to
generate product 3 and regenerate two metal catalysts.

C onclusion
Three protocols have been described for the highly diaster-
eo- and enantioselective hydrophosphinylation of allenes,
1,3-enynes and conjugated dienes via Pd/Co dual catalysis.
Two types of motifs bearing both a P- and C-stereocenter or
both a P-stereocenter and chiral axis are prepared in good
yields and with excellent regio-, diastereo-, and enantiose-
lectivities. A modified P(V) compound as a masked
unsymmetric phosphinylating reagent is critical to the
achievement of high stereoselectivities for the transforma-
tion. The unreported stereodivergent hydrophosphinylation
reaction is also realized to access all four stereoisomers of
phosphinylated allenes. In addition, the reaction features a
very short reaction time and low catalyst loading and can be
run on gram-scale, all of which make this protocol powerful
and practically valuable. Preliminary mechanistic experi-
ments elucidate the role of two catalysts and suggest the
involvement of kinetic resolution and reductive elimination
in the catalytic cycle.

Diastereoselective and Enantioselective Hydrophosphinylations of
Conjugated Enynes, Allenes and Dienes via Synergistic Pd/Co
Catalysis
Ming-Qiao Tang, Zi-Jiang Yang, Ai-Jun Han, and Zhi-Tao He*

Abstract: Different from the reported work focusing on
the construction of single P- or C-stereocenter via
hydrophosphinylation of unsaturated carbon bonds, the
highly diastereo- and enantioselective hydrophosphiny-
lation reaction of allenes, conjugated enynes and 1,3-
dienes is achieved via a designed Pd/Co dual catalysis
and newly modified masked phosphinylating reagent. A
series of allyl motifs bearing both a tertiary C- and
P-stereocenter are prepared in generally good yields,
>20: 1 dr, >20: 1 rr and 99% ee. The unprecedented
diastereo- and enantioselective hydrophosphinylation of
1,3-enynes is established to generate skeletons contain-
ing both a P-stereocenter and a nonadjacent chiral axis.
The first stereodivergent hydrophosphinylation reaction
is also developed to achieve all four P-containing stereo-
isomers. The present protocol features the use of only
3-minutes reaction time and 0.1 % catalyst, and with the
observation of up to 730 TON. A set of mechanistic
studies reveal the necessity and roles of two metal
catalysts and corroborate the designed synergistic proc-
ess.
Introduction

Enantioenriched organophosphorus motifs have been widely
used in chiral ligand and catalyst design, medicinal and
material chemistry.<sup>[1]</sup> In addition to various catalytic path-
ways such as 1,4-conjugate addition, allylic substitution,
cross coupling, nucleophilic substitution and others,<sup>[2]</sup> the
asymmetric hydrophosphinylation and hydrophosphination

of unsaturated carbon-carbon bonds have emerged as a
valuable and convenient route to construct these
skeletons.<sup>[3–9]</sup> For example, in 2018, Dong reported the first
Pd-catalyzed asymmetric hydrophosphinylation of unacti-
vated 1,3-dienes.<sup>[4b]</sup> Wang and Li extended hydrophosphina-
tion and hydrophosphinylation to the use of allenes with
high enantiocontrol.<sup>[4h,i]</sup> However, these works focus exclu-
sively on the construction of P- or C-stereocenter and fail to
provide high stereocontrol on both of them simultaneously
(Scheme 1a). A few prior works tried to establish the related
diastereoselective processes but generally furnished 1: 1
diastereoselectivity for the transformations.<sup>[4h,l,5b,f,8]</sup> Only an
elegant work by Li and co-workers describes diastereoselec-
tive access to phosphine-functionalized olefins via Pd-
catalyzed hydrophosphination of alkynes.<sup>[4i]</sup> Thus, the route
to achieve diastereo- and enantioselective hydrophosphiny-
lation and hydrophosphination reactions is still rare. Mean-
while, the asymmetric hydrofunctionalization of 1,3-enynes
is a facile route to prepare enantioenriched allenes,<sup>[10,11]</sup> but
related hydrophosphinylation and hydrophosphination proc-
esses remain undeveloped, neither enantioselectively nor
diastereoselectively.

Stereodivergent synthesis has received much attention
due to the potential to achieve all the stereoisomers of a
constructed skeleton.<sup>[12]</sup> However, all the reported studies
focus on the construction of C-based stereocenters, and
seldomly explore the involvement of heteroatom-based
stereocenter (Scheme 1b). Obviously, heteroatom-based
stereodivergent synthesis represents a new direction in this
area and would greatly extend the concept of stereo-
divergent synthesis. Therefore, stereodivergent hydrophos-
phinylation and hydrophosphination reaction to prepare P-
involved chiral motifs are unknown.

Synergistic catalysis has shown great potential in control-
ling multiple stereocenters in the stereoselective synthesis.<sup>[13]</sup>
Recently, Duan et al. reported an interesting study toward
the preparation of P-stereocenter via Co-catalyzed 1,4-
addition and nucleophilic substitution with racemic
phosphine oxides.<sup>[14]</sup> Inspired by this work and considering
the high efficiency of Pd-catalyzed asymmetric
hydrofunctionalizations,<sup>[15–18]</sup> we envisioned that a synergistic
Pd/Co catalytic system might provide a novel solution to this
long-standing unsolved diastereoselective hydrophosphiny-
lation to construct motifs bearing both a P- and C-stereo-
center. Meanwhile, with the precise dictation of Pd and Co
catalysts on related coupling partners, the stereodivergent

hydrophosphinylation reaction to access all four P-contain-

Herein, we describe our endeavors to establish three
types of diastereo- and enantioselective hydrophosphinyla-
tion transformations via a synergistic Pd/Co catalysis
(Scheme 1c). With allene and newly modified masked P(V)
reagent as the substrates, the hydrophosphinylation can be
realized to generate skeletons bearing both a P- and
C-stereocenter. The hydrophosphinylation of 1,3-enynes is
also developed to furnish motifs containing a P-stereocenter
and a chiral axis. This protocol is further applied to the
unprecedented diastereoselective hydrophosphinylation of
conjugated diene. In addition, a stereodivergent protocol is
described to access all of the stereoisomers of the con-
structed P-containing units.
Results and Discussion

With this design in mind, aryloxyallene 1a and pyridyl
phosphine oxide 2a-1 were selected as the electrophile and
nucleophile, respectively (Table 1). When BINAP L5 was
selected as the chiral ligand for Pd catalyst, a set of chiral
ligands for Co metal was evaluated first. With Boxmi ligand
L1 used,<sup>[19]</sup> the synergistic catalysis occurred and provided
3a in 36% yield and 60 % ee but with 1.4: 1 dr (entry 1).
When a similar ligand L2 was used instead, both the
reactivity and stereocontrol were increased obviously. In
this case, 77% yield, 4.5:1 dr and 79 % ee for product 3 a
were observed (entry 2). Other chiral ligands did not show
better stereocontrol for the hydrofunctionalization process
(see Supporting Information for details). Next, a group of
chiral ligands instead of L5 for Pd metal was checked
(entries 3–9). Among them, L10 exhibited the optimal

results, furnishing 3a in 75 % yield, 11: 1 dr and 96% ee. A
series of other condition evaluations including different
bases and solvents were conducted. The corresponding
results were summarized in the Supporting Information but
all failed to provide superior effects.

Murakami et al. demonstrated that an α-hydroxyalkyl-
phosphonate as the masked phosphonating reagent could
prevent catalyst deactivation and presumably have a positive
influence on reactivity and selectivity.<sup>[20]</sup> Several modified

the reaction of 2a-1 and ketones. We found that these new
phosphonating reagents are actually much easier to be
prepared and purified than that for 2a-1. With 2 a used
instead of 2a-1 (entry 10), indeed both the diastereoselectiv-
ity and enantioselectivity of 3 a were elevated (from 11 : 1 to
>20 :1 dr and 96 % to 97 % ee). Similarly, 2a-2 and 2a-3 as
masked 2a-1 showed excellent stereocontrol effects and
with slightly decreased yields for 3a (entries 11–12). When
the reaction temperature was lowered to room temperature,
3a was achieved in the highest 71% yield, >20 :1 dr and

be noted that, in this context, if ent-L2 was adopted instead

Conclusion

Three protocols have been described for the highly diaster-
eo- and enantioselective hydrophosphinylation of allenes,
1,3-enynes and conjugated dienes via Pd/Co dual catalysis.
Two types of motifs bearing both a P- and C-stereocenter or
both a P-stereocenter and chiral axis are prepared in good
yields and with excellent regio-, diastereo-, and enantiose-
lectivities. A modified P(V) compound as a masked
unsymmetric phosphinylating reagent is critical to the
achievement of high stereoselectivities for the transforma-
tion. The unreported stereodivergent hydrophosphinylation
reaction is also realized to access all four stereoisomers of
phosphinylated allenes. In addition, the reaction features a
very short reaction time and low catalyst loading and can be
run on gram-scale, all of which make this protocol powerful
and practically valuable. Preliminary mechanistic experi-
ments elucidate the role of two catalysts and suggest the
involvement of kinetic resolution and reductive elimination
in the catalytic cycle.
